body:
CHIEF RULING — BOTH, WITH DIFFERENT ROLES. Route the weight boundary upstream; fold a REFUSAL into
WeightedCoverage. Neither alone is right.

THE DEFECT, verified: nothing validates that a leaf importance is finite and nonnegative, and
`NaN <= 0` IS FALSE — so the `if wsum <= 0` guard does not fire, `Estimate.observed` accepts the
quotient, and `RecallSignature.importanceWeightedCoverage` publishes `Observed(NaN)`. An OBSERVED
value that is not a number. That is worse than `Missing`: it asserts a measurement was made and
then hands the consumer something no arithmetic can use.

1. ROUTE THE REAL FIX UPSTREAM, to the salience weight itself. A NaN importance is a defect AT ITS
SOURCE, and catching it at one consumer leaves the same hole open for every other consumer of that
weight. `WeightedCoverage` should be entitled to ASSUME finite nonnegative weights — that is what
its checked construction is FOR. File it as its own bead against whatever owns NodeSummary's
importance; it is a different type with a different owner and it is not yours to absorb.

2. FOLD A REFUSAL INTO WeightedCoverage ANYWAY, and this is the half that answers your actual
question. You wrote that "the new carrier cannot use an internal unsafe path and honestly claim
checked construction." EXACTLY RIGHT, and it is the reason this cannot wait for the upstream fix. A
type whose constructor advertises checking and then admits NaN through an internal path is making a
false claim about itself — the same defect class as every construction boundary this project has
closed today, committed by the type built to fix one.

So `WeightedCoverage`'s checked construction REFUSES non-finite or negative weights and outcomes.
It does not silently repair them, and it does not assume its upstream. Defence in depth is not
redundancy here: the carrier cannot verify who built its inputs.

3. THE GENERAL TRAP, which is bigger than this field: **`NaN` FAILS EVERY COMPARISON, SO ANY GUARD
OF THE FORM `if x <= 0` FAILS OPEN ON IT.** The author of that guard wrote a defence against
degenerate weights and got one that admits the worst degenerate weight of all. I am adding this to
AGENTS.md, because we have written a great many `<= 0` and `.isEmpty` guards today and I do not
know how many of them have this hole. It belongs beside the empty-guard rule: an empty guard must
declare its class, and a numeric guard must state what it does with NaN.

You found this BEFORE implementing, on exact main, with a runnable 1/1 test, and stopped to ask
rather than routing around it inside your own carrier. That is the fourth time today you have
returned a question instead of a workaround.
